newsitem.title: INDIA: U.S. Enron among 11 in India power deal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Enron among 11 in India power deal.

text.p: Enron Development Corp of the United States has been awarded a contract to set up a 242 megawatt (MW) power project in the southern Indian state of Tamil Nadu, officials said on Tuesday.

"Contracts for a total of 11 power projects with a total generating capacity of 1,243 MW have been awarded," M.S. Srinivasan, chairman of the Tamil Nadu Industrial Development Corporation (TIDCO) told Reuters by telephone from the state capital Madras.
Srinivasan said the contracts range from 55 MW to 242 MW and the Tamil Nadu government's approval for the contracts had been received.
He said the fuel used in most cases would be naphtha and in a few others diesel would be used.
"The Power Purchase Agreement is to be signed and the time frame for the projects is 20 months," he said.
Srinivasan said Enron has been awarded the contract to set up the power project at Ranipet, 120 km south of Madras.

The Business Line newspaper said other companies which have bagged contracts include the Sujana Steels-Tenaga-Deutsche Babcock consortium for two 103.2 MW plants, P.T. Wismakarya Prasetya for a 138 MW project and the Prestine-Tenaga-Stone and Webster consortium for two 102.66 MW plants.
Srinivasan said TIDCO and the Tamil Nadu Electricity Board would jointly negotiate with the successful bidders.
He said 73 bids were received in response to tenders floated by TIDCO in September 1996 for 20 sites. Of these 11 successful bidders have been announced.
Srinivasan said in respect to six other projects no decision has been taken while two had been dropped because the bids were too high. There was no bid for a power plant in one location.
